title: 'Theme Types'
description: 'The palette that makes up a theme: semantic colors, raw colors, and the base type.'

### Where a theme lives

A theme is a folder holding two files: its [`manifest.json`](/addons/manifest) and a **`bundle.json`** holding the definition below. The bundle's name is fixed. The loader looks for exactly `bundle.json` beside the manifest, and skips the theme if the file is missing or doesn't parse into a JSON object.

<Warning>
	Unlike plugins, themes **ignore the manifest's `main` field**. It's still required for the manifest to validate, but nothing reads it when locating the bundle. If your colors aren't applying, check the file is named `bundle.json`, not whatever `main` points at.
</Warning>

### The shape of a theme

A theme definition has three parts that decide its colors: a base `type`, a set of `semantic` colors, and a set of `raw` colors. Together they override Discord's palette.

```json bundle.json
{
	"type": "darker",
	"semantic": { },
	"raw": { },
	"background": { }
}
```

### Base type

`type` picks the foundation your theme builds on. You only override the colors you care about, and everything else falls back to this base.

<Tabs>
	<Tab title='midnight'>
		A pure-black base, for OLED/AMOLED-style themes.
	</Tab>
	<Tab title='darker'>
		A dark base, deeper than Discord's default dark.
	</Tab>
	<Tab title='light'>
		A light base.
	</Tab>
</Tabs>

### Semantic colors

**Semantic** colors are Discord's named roles: `BACKGROUND_PRIMARY`, `TEXT_NORMAL`, and so on. Theming by role means a single value recolors everywhere that role is used, so the result stays consistent across the app.

Each key is the **selector name** of the color Unbound hooks. A key that doesn't match any selector is inert: it's never looked up, and nothing warns you about it.

Each entry is an object: a `type` of `color` (a literal color) or `raw` (a reference to a raw color), the `value`, and an optional `opacity`.

```ts
semantic: {
	BACKGROUND_PRIMARY: { type: 'color', value: '#0c0c0c' },
	TEXT_NORMAL:        { type: 'color', value: '#fcfcfc', opacity: 1 },
}
```

<ResponseField name='type' type="'color' | 'raw'">
	`color` is a literal value; `raw` points at one of your raw colors so many roles can share it.
</ResponseField>
<ResponseField name='value' type='string'>
	The color, or the raw key when `type` is `raw`.
</ResponseField>
<ResponseField name='opacity' type='number'>
	Optional opacity from `0` to `1`, applied on top of the parsed color. It replaces any alpha the color string already carried, and is ignored when `type` is `raw`.
</ResponseField>

An entry missing `type` or `value` is skipped and the role keeps its original color.

### Raw colors

**Raw** colors are a flat map keyed by the **selector name** of a system color, such as `systemBlueColor`. Setting one replaces that color everywhere the app asks for it, below the level of Discord's roles. Point semantic roles at one with `type: 'raw'` and they share whatever it resolves to.

```json
{
	"raw": {
		"systemBlueColor": "#c74050"
	},
	"semantic": {
		"BUTTON_BACKGROUND": { "type": "raw", "value": "systemBlueColor" }
	}
}
```

Raw overrides are swapped in when the theme is applied and restored when you switch away, so only the applied theme's raw colors are ever in effect.

<Tip>
	Put your brand colors in `raw` and wire `semantic` roles to them. It keeps a theme DRY, so one edit recolors everything that shares a value.
</Tip>

### Color formats

Every color string, in `raw` or in a semantic `color` entry, is parsed the same way. Three formats are accepted:

<ParamField path='#RRGGBB' type='hex'>
	Six-digit hex. Alpha is treated as fully opaque.
</ParamField>
<ParamField path='#RRGGBBAA' type='hex'>
	Eight-digit hex, with alpha as the final byte (`00` to `FF`).
</ParamField>
<ParamField path='rgb(r, g, b)' type='function'>
	Three channels, each `0` to `255`. Fully opaque.
</ParamField>
<ParamField path='rgba(r, g, b, a)' type='function'>
	Three channels `0` to `255`, plus alpha.
</ParamField>

<Warning>
	In `rgba`, **alpha is a `0` to `1` fraction while `r`, `g` and `b` are `0` to `255`.** Writing `rgba(255, 0, 0, 255)` does not give you opaque red, and a `0` alpha silently renders the color fully transparent rather than failing. Use `rgba(255, 0, 0, 1)`.
</Warning>

An `rgba` string with fewer than four values, or an `rgb` string with fewer than three, fails to parse, as does any string that doesn't start with `#`, `rgb`, or `rgba`. Named CSS colors like `red` are not supported.

<Note>
	A color that fails to parse is not an error you'll see. Unbound falls back to the original color for that entry and the app keeps rendering, so a malformed value looks like an override that simply didn't apply. Check the format first when a color won't take.
</Note>

See [Creating an Addon](/addons/creating) for building and installing a theme, and [The Manifest](/addons/manifest) for the metadata that ships beside the bundle.
